A second US trial (605 people aged 65+, one centre; everyone had an assessment, only one group had a specialist team act on it): serious side effects 51 vs 61 in 100; no clear difference in admissions or survival. US guidance recommends assessment for everyone over 65 with cancer. UK specialists report few patients can get it.
Li et al., JAMA Oncol 2021; Dale et al., JCO 2023; Gomes et al., J Geriatr Oncol 2024
alt_text: Checklist of seven things a geriatric assessment covers before cancer treatment at 70+: daily function, falls, memory, mood, nutrition, medicines, support at home.

Bars from a US trial of 718 people aged 70+ with incurable cancer. Serious side effects over 3 months: about 51 in 100 with assessment vs 71 in 100 usual care. Falls: about 12 vs 21 in 100. Survival was similar; the trial was not designed to test it.

Text card on dark teal: ask the cancer team if an assessment is possible. A second US trial of 605 people found serious side effects 51 vs 61 in 100, with no clear difference in admissions or survival. UK specialists report few patients can get it.
